name: Make mayonnaise by hand
blurb: An emulsion made from egg yolk, oil and acid — a five-minute lesson in the technique that also underpins hollandaise, aioli and vinaigrette.
gear: A bowl and a whisk, or a stick blender
Egg yolks, neutral oil, lemon juice or vinegar, mustard, salt
steps: Set the bowl on a damp cloth so it cannot spin, and whisk the yolk with mustard, a little acid and salt.
Add the oil drop by drop at first, whisking constantly. This is where emulsions are made or broken.
Once it thickens and takes, you can pour the oil in a slow, thin stream.
Adjust at the end with acid, salt and a splash of water to reach the consistency you want.
Learn the rescue: if it splits, start with a fresh yolk in a clean bowl and whisk the broken mixture into it drop by drop.
Make a flavoured version — aioli with garlic, or a herb mayonnaise.
tips: Adding oil too fast is the only real way to fail. Slower than feels reasonable.
Room-temperature ingredients emulsify far more readily than fridge-cold ones.
Raw egg carries a small salmonella risk. Use very fresh or pasteurised eggs, and avoid serving it to anyone vulnerable.
proof: A thick, glossy, stable mayonnaise made by hand, plus one successful rescue of a deliberately split batch.
